# Measurable assembly of density-controlled barycentric repairs

This note closes the measurable-selection issue when a pointwise repair
theorem has already been proved on almost every normal face. It does not
prove the missing geometric density compatibility for arbitrary convex
surface disintegrations. The construction is elementary and uses compact
metric spaces and countably many continuous constraints.

## 1. A compact measurable selection lemma

Let T be a standard Borel space and X a compact metric space. Suppose
f_j:T times X -> R, j>=1, are Borel functions, continuous in x for each
fixed t. Assume every set

    F(t)={x in X: f_j(t,x)<=0 for every j}

is nonempty. Then F has a Borel selector.

**Proof.** Fix a countable dense sequence (x_l) in X. For each k choose
the least l for which

    max_(j<=k) f_j(t,x_l)<1/k.

Such an l exists: a point of F(t) has an open neighborhood satisfying
these finitely many strict inequalities. The least-index choice x_k(t)
is Borel. Any cluster point of a subsequence with indices tending to
infinity lies in F(t), by continuity of each f_j(t,.) at that fixed t.

Here is a Borel way to choose a cluster point. For each m fix a finite
closed cover C_(m,1),...,C_(m,Nm) of X with every member of diameter at
most 2^(-m). At stage one choose the least l_1 for which infinitely many
x_k(t) belong to C_(1,l_1). At stage m choose the least l_m for which
infinitely many x_k(t) belong to

    D_m(t)=intersection_(a<=m) C_(a,l_a(t)).

The choice exists, since a finite cover of a set containing infinitely
many terms has one member containing infinitely many of them. Each
infinite-occurrence condition is Borel: it is the countable statement
that for every N there is k>=N with membership in the specified finitely
many closed sets. Induction gives Borel finite-valued l_m(t).

The compact sets D_m(t) are nested, nonempty, and have diameter at most
2^(-m). Choose the least k_m(t)>=m with x_(k_m(t))(t) in D_m(t). This
is Borel, and the resulting points converge to the unique point of
intersection_m D_m(t). The limit is Borel, is a cluster point along
indices tending to infinity, and therefore belongs to F(t). QED.

The same conclusion holds outside a Borel null set, with any arbitrary
fixed value assigned on that set. No continuity of t->F(t), optimizer
uniqueness, or unproved interchange of limits is needed.

## 2. Application to face couplings

Fix a compact physical set B and a Borel normal parameter t. Suppose
gamma_(i,t), rho_(old,t), and sigma_t are Borel finite-measure kernels
with uniformly bounded masses, all supported in fixed compact sets.
The gamma_(i,t) have the same mass for each t. Let b be the continuous
barycentric map with fixed weights. Suppose for every relevant t there
exists a coupling pi with these marginals satisfying

    rho_(old,t)<=_cx b_*pi,       b_*pi<=sigma_t.     (1)

Then such couplings can be selected as a Borel kernel t->pi_t.

To apply Section 1, take X to be the compact space of positive measures
of mass at most the common uniform bound on the compact product B^k.
Marginal equalities can be imposed using absolute differences of
integrals against a countable dense family of continuous functions on
B, including the constant one. Measure domination can be imposed
using a countable uniformly dense family of nonnegative continuous
functions on the compact output set. These yield Borel-in-t,
continuous-in-pi inequalities.

Convex order also requires only countably many tests. Finite maxima of
affine functions with rational coefficients form a countable family.
Any finite convex function on the ambient Euclidean space is uniformly
approximated on the compact output set by functions in this family:
choose a finite supporting-affine approximation on a surrounding compact
ball and approximate its finitely many coefficients by rationals. Mass
and first moments are already fixed by the marginals. Thus inequalities
for that countable family imply all the convex comparisons in (1).

These countable continuous constraints define a nonempty compact set
in X for every t. Section 1 supplies the required Borel kernel. If input
supports depend on t, the prescribed marginals enforce those supports;
no separate moving-support closed-graph assumption is required.

Integrating pi_t against the normal reference measure gives one physical
tuple measure. Every fiberwise convex-order comparison and density
domination integrates to its full joint version. If the pointwise tuple
midpoints belong to the actual middle face, this physical support
condition also persists under integration.

## 3. Measurable reconstruction of a two-endpoint midpoint martingale

In this section there are two endpoints of equal weights 1/2. Suppose
pointwise repair gives rho_(old,t)<=_cx rho_t and the original
middle source law nu_t satisfies

    nu_t<=_cx eta_t+2rho_(old,t).

Assume the measures form Borel kernels of bounded mass on common compact
sets. Then nu_t<=_cx eta_t+2rho_t. Compact convex-order martingale
existence gives a martingale at each t, as in the already audited
reconstruction theorem. These martingales can be selected measurably
using Section 1 again: the constraints are the two marginal equalities
and

    integral a(x)(y_l-x_l) dPi_t(x,y)=0

for every coordinate l and every a in a countable dense family of
continuous functions on the source compact set. These constraints
are continuous in Pi_t and Borel in t; they express precisely the
conditional barycenter identity.

Integrate the selected martingale kernels in t. Tag its joint target
measure eta_t+2rho_t as an eta branch or a 2rho branch using the joint
Radon--Nikodym decomposition on (t,point); the two nonnegative densities
sum to one almost everywhere. Disintegrate the joint selected endpoint
tuple measure over (t,midpoint), and split the 2rho branch into its two
endpoints with probabilities 1/2 and 1/2. Keep the eta branch intact. The
composition retains the original source, the prescribed middle and
endpoint target marginals, and the normal parameter. The midpoint is
the mean of the last split, so the full composition is a martingale.

This proves that a continuum of normals is not an additional selection
obstacle once the pointwise conditional density theorem is available.
It supplies no such theorem for an arbitrary Borel face foliation.
